content.comment_body: Hello, I am a postgraduate student seeking to use [product_name] for my automation project. I purchased a USB [product_name] cable from eBay (see attached product photo). Now, I'm looking to buy a [product_name] that can be programmed with this cable, and would appreciate specific guidance on which [version_no] to choose. I need to ensure the [product_name] is compatible with my USB cable and not other programming interfaces. Also, please advise on the minimum [product_name] software version required for programming the model you recommend and the USB cable I have. Many thanks in advance.
Apologies, the attachment is included here.

This cable is needed only for programming older [product_name] models. The most recent version is [version_no]. For [product_name] with [version_no], an Ethernet cable is sufficient for programming. The suitable [product_name] depends on your project requirements. There are four main types, both with and without display. For reference, see the release note at [url]. For programming, you'll need [product_name] software version [version_no].

Sorry, attaching the file now. The image 'plccable.jpg' shows the cable labeled [product_name]. Please review the image and advise if the cable should be returned (in case it isn't usable with [version_no] [product_name]). Another commenter mentioned being in a similar situation, possibly from the same educational institution.

Thank you all for the quick responses. My issue is slightly different. I bought the [product_name] cable from eBay without prior knowledge of PLCs, based on my supervisor’s advice to get a [product_name] unit and cable. I bought the cable first due to limited availability at the time. After researching drivers for the cable, I learned that modern [product_name] units (like [version_no]) do not require this cable, as no compatible port exists. I discovered this after reading other posts. Now, I have two choices: either discard the USB cable (since eBay won't accept returns), or purchase an older [product_name] version that supports programming with my cable so my investment isn't wasted. Since I spent my own money, I prefer not to throw it away. Please tell me which older [version_no] [product_name] models work with this cable, so I buy only a compatible device. My use case is simple (basic motor control by logic/switches; no advanced features needed). I've attached images of my USB cable for reference. Vendors have offered me devices like [article_no]—images attached. It was an oversight not asking earlier, but I want to double-check future purchases. Please help—I'm quite concerned. Thank you in advance.

The provided pictures show older versions of both the cables and [product_name]. One photo features a very obsolete [product_name] ([article_no]), rarely found outside museums. I wouldn't recommend using such outdated hardware, even if free. The cable is suitable for versions up to [article_no]. One question remains: why did you reach out to the forum only after purchasing the cable instead of seeking advice beforehand?

"You can use the cable with [product_name] versions up to [article_no]"—does this mean it’s compatible with any model up to [article_no], but not later versions? I want to confirm before buying. I realize it was a mistake not to ask about compatibility first, but now the cable can't be returned. I want to ensure I buy an old [product_name] that works with the cable, and not repeat the error by purchasing an incompatible device. Thank you.

The last digit in the order number is crucial; [product_name] started from [article_no] upwards. The newest model is [version_no] ([article_no]), but note that programming [product_name] [version_no] and [version_no] uses Ethernet. Hope this helps clarify.

If buying a used PLC, consider options between [version_no] and [version_no]. Older units aren’t recommended. New units are preferable, since used devices might have worn relay outputs. For basic logic tasks, a [version_no] is ideal and future upgrades to [version_no] can be considered. Do keep in mind that extension cards for newer models won’t work with the older types. Hope this assists you.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum members experience confusion regarding compatibility between USB programming cables and legacy [product_name] versions. Users struggle to identify which older models can be programmed with non-original cables and are frustrated by post-purchase incompatibility. Concerns also arise about the required software versions and the difficulty locating older, suitable hardware—leading to anxiety about possibly losing their investment.
analysis.user_expectations: The user hopes to use a previously purchased USB programming cable with a compatible [product_name] version and wants clear, reliable advice on which hardware and software combinations will work. They aim to avoid further spending or wasted purchases and seek detailed guidance before making any decisions.
